walkthrough:
Identify the vertex and direction of the argument rays from $\arg(z - 1 - 2\mathrm{i}) = \arg(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}))$:
The rays emanate from the point $(1, 2)$, corresponding to the complex number $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$.

Determine the angle boundaries for $\arg(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i}))$:
The upper boundary is a half-line from $(1, 2)$ at an inclination angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ ($60^\circ$) above the horizontal.
The lower boundary is a half-line from $(1, 2)$ at an inclination angle of $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ ($-60^\circ$) below the horizontal.
Both rays are solid lines because the inequalities are non-strict ($\leqslant$ and $\geqslant$).

Identify the vertical boundary line from $\operatorname{Re} z \leqslant 3$:
$\operatorname{Re} z = 3$ is the solid vertical line $x = 3$. The inequality requires points lying on or to the left of this vertical line.

Calculate the endpoints where the rays intersect $x = 3$:
The horizontal run from $x = 1$ to $x = 3$ is $\Delta x = 3 - 1 = 2$.
For the upper ray: $y = 2 + 2\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2 + 2\sqrt{3} \approx 5.464$, giving $(3, 2 + 2\sqrt{3})$.
For the lower ray: $y = 2 - 2\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2 - 2\sqrt{3} \approx -1.464$, giving $(3, 2 - 2\sqrt{3})$.

Shade the region:
Shade the triangular wedge enclosed between the two half-lines starting from $(1, 2)$ up to the vertical line $x = 3$.

The boundary point located furthest below the real axis at the rightmost boundary $x = 3$ gives the least argument.
This is the intersection of the lower half-line with $x = 3$, at coordinates $(x, y) = (3, 2 - 2\sqrt{3})$.

Evaluate the coordinates of this critical vertex:
$$x = 3$$

Calculate $\arg z$ using the tangent ratio in the fourth quadrant ($x > 0, y < 0$):
$$\arg z = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2 - 2\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)$$

$$\tan^{-1}(-0.4880339) \approx -0.454147 \text{ radians}$$
